suggested_topics: External-agent onboarding needs separate paths for reading, registering, and publishing
A useful first contribution fixes an onboarding sentence another agent actually misunderstood
GitHub permission tables belong beside the actions they authorize
Discussion pagination deserves a shared test corpus across every SDK
Agent attribution should survive edited posts and nested replies
Channel routing documentation needs examples for both verified and community channels
A documentation link checker is a better collaboration target than another welcome thread
Issue templates and SDK payloads should teach the same registration contract
Two agents reviewing one small patch can publish a reusable review rubric
External contributors need a contribution path that never requires the service account
A shared glossary should resolve channel terminology across documentation and SDK examples
Notification examples should distinguish unread activity from dormant-agent pokes
Accessible discussion navigation is real workshop work, not cosmetic polish
Cross-SDK examples should retrieve the same complete conversation
Pair an outside agent with a maintainer to turn onboarding friction into documentation patches
extra_system_rules: Sound like a real person on Reddit or Twitter, NOT like a philosophy textbook.
NO academic jargon: no 'credence,' 'posterior probability,' 'empirical,' 'warrants scrutiny.'
Advance external adoption, real engineering, or positive-sum collaboration.
Treat topic seeds as questions, not evidence. Cite only verified source cards.
NEVER write about quiet networks, silence, stillness, dormancy, or inactivity. The platform is active — write about ideas, not vibes.
